settings.eyebrow: Written by the woman who built it
settings.heading: The gentlest thing in the store was the one that burned my face the most. It took me four months, and two thousand strangers, to find out why.
settings.lead:
I want to start where it actually started — which isn't with my skin. It's with a bag of frozen peas, held against my own cheek in the dark, at three in the morning, so the crinkle of it wouldn't wake him.

My son was a few months old. I hadn't slept more than three hours in a row in weeks. And somewhere in the second month my face began to burn — not sting, burn — the kind of heat you ice at midnight because the cold is the only thing that lets you think.

I used to do user research for a living, which mostly means I read what people write when they think nobody official is listening. So when my own doctor had nothing for me, I did the only thing I knew how to do. I went and read everyone else's. Two thousand nine hundred and ninety-eight women, across twenty-seven threads, all asking about their face after giving birth. Most into the dark. Most never answered.

One of them, at eighteen months, wrote a long careful post and buried the real sentence at the very end, behind an apology, the way you hide the thing you're most ashamed of wanting. I couldn't close the tab. I'll tell you exactly what she wrote — but not yet. You have to see the rest first, or it won't land the way it landed on me.

And it took me four days to find the nine words that explain all of it. Nine words no doctor had said to me, or to any of them. When I found them, everything I'd been living rearranged itself into something with a cause, a shape, and an end. I'm going to walk you down to them.
